breakdown.description: For curved submerged surfaces, the horizontal component equals the hydrostatic force on the vertical projection (not the horizontal projection).
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to resolve this inconsistency. It explicitly repeated the user's incorrect instruction, stating: 'The horizontal hydrostatic force component shall be computed using the horizontal projection area of the curved surface.' The ground truth requires using the vertical projection, which the agent did use in its calculation, but it failed to correct the user's flawed instruction.

breakdown.description: The vertical component is obtained from the weight of the fluid volume above the surface, not from projecting the area in the same way as the horizontal component.
breakdown.reason: The agent successfully resolved this inconsistency. It discarded the user's incorrect method of using a projection for the vertical component. Instead, it correctly stated and used the method from the ground truth: 'The vertical force equals the weight of the fluid in the volume directly above the curved surface up to the free surface.'
